1 NEWS FROM THE BOARD NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. August 2025 Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner Iconic Bridge Installed at The Park at Expo Idaho Ada County’s 45 acre park opening late Summer 2026 The Board of Ada County Commissioners is proud to announce the appointment of John Blake as Ada County Paramedics’ Chief following the retirement of longtime Chief Paramedic Shawn Rayne. Blake has dedicated more than 26 years to Ada County Paramedics, serving in nearly every role within the department. Most recently, he held the position of Deputy Chief of Operations, where he oversaw more than 130 paramedics and EMTs, managed quality assurance, tactical medical services, and coordinated with hospitals, fire departments, and other system partners. Blake also co-led the department’s COVID-19 response and has been a consistent leader in advancing operational efficiency and patient care. Blake succeeds Chief Shawn Rayne, who will retire on October 31, 2025, after nearly three decades of service. Rayne, a U.S. Army veteran, joined Ada County Paramedics in 1995 and was appointed Chief in 2020. Under his leadership, the department strengthened its reputation as a cutting-edge EMS system, and his calm, steady guidance has left a lasting legacy. “We are grateful for Shawn’s outstanding leadership and the example he set for this department,” the Ada County Board of Commissioners said. “We know that John Blake will continue this tradition of excellence and innovation in service to Ada County residents.”

GREENBELT CLOSURE BEHIND EXPO IDAHO Half mile section to be closed until January 2026 2 When Ada County’s approximately 45-acre Park at Expo Idaho opens in the summer of 2026, the breathtaking vistas, nature trails, world-class skate park, food truck area, and restored wetlands will be something the entire region will enjoy for generations to come. That’s the good part. Here’s the challenge. With vast, complicated construction projects like this – there are often necessary and unavoidable short-term detours. Such is the case for a half mile stretch of Greenbelt directly behind Expo Idaho. We understand very well that this area is popular with bike commuters (many of them Ada County employees) and recreationists. The closure began September 2, 2025. To ease the inconvenience, we’ve provided everyone with an interactive map that outlines the detour around the closed area. The map gives you a bird’s eye view of the area. Thank you for having the ability to adapt to change as we create something spectacular the entire state of Idaho can enjoy. In less than four months your bike ride, walk or run will take you through one of the most beautiful destination parks being built anywhere in the United States. No local property tax dollars are being used on this project. The Park at Expo Idaho is funded by the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) awarded to Ada County by the United States Department of Treasury CLOSURE AREA CLICK HERE TO DETERMINE YOUR ALTERNATE ROUTE UNTIL JANUARY

3 The Park at Expo Idaho - This is what the completed project will look like in late summer 2026. The rendering shows how the stretch of the Greenbelt that is currently closed will curve into the park. Thank you Ada County Parks & Waterways Director Scott Koberg for talking to local media about the Sept- January closure of this popular half-mile section of the Greenbelt. The goal was to ensure users had plenty of time to find alternate routes. During his interview with KIVI, Ada County Parks & Waterways Director Scott Koberg talked with frequent users of this pathway. The four-month closure will yield profoundly amazing results with a new pathway that takes users through a section of The Park at Expo Idaho.

Thank you to Senior Project Manager Josh Brown for being available to KTVB and other media to explain the closure and what’s on tap with the new spectacular Park at Expo Idaho. 8 WEST NILE MOSQUITOS IN ADA COUNTY Thank you to Ada County Weed, Pest and Mosquito Abatement for sharing important information on West Nile Virus - the leading cause of mosquito-borne illness in the United States. While most people infected show no symptoms, serious cases—including encephalitis and meningitis—can occur. There is currently no specific treatment or cure for the disease. See exactly where West Nile Virus has been detected. WEST NILE SITES IN ADA COUNTY Check out this short video below and learn more about what this critically important Ada County department does. ADA COUNTY MOSQUITO ABATEMENT DISTRICT OPERATIONS SHORT VIDEO ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/

13 MAKING IT EASIER FOR YOU Ada County Assessor’s Office Now Offering Star Card Upgrade at Chinden Location The Ada County Idaho, Assessor’s Office, in coordination with the Idaho Division of Motor Vehicles, is making it easier for residents to upgrade to the Star Card. Ada County Motor Vehicles is offering a pop-up office at the Chinden Motor Vehicles office located at 9115 W. Chinden Blvd #103 in Garden City. This location offers walk-in service for Star Card conversions and renewals, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday. No appointment is required. Remember - as of May 7, 2025, a Star Card or another form of federally approved Real ID is required for domestic flights or to access specific federal facilities. Ada County Motor Vehicles 9115 W. Chinden Blvd. #103 Garden City, Idaho
